title: Probabilistic charge model for multi-stage rerank and toolcall pipelines
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Background: Modern non-chat pipelines at Redwood often execute multi-stage rerank flows: an initial embeddings fanout -> candidate scoring -> optional downstream function/tool calls (e.g., external search, enrichment). Current meter semantics charge deterministically for every stage that ran, which leads to overcharging in two realistic cases: 1) speculative upstream retries or duplicate RPCs from transient network errors, and 2) downstream conditional toolcalls that are optimistic (attempted but later cancelled or short-circuited).

Scope: design and implement a probabilistic / confidence-weighted charging model that: (a) attributes fractional charge for tentative work when downstream completion is uncertain, (b) ensures ledger atomicity for finalized executions, (c) reconciles idempotent retries and duplicate event deliveries to avoid double-billing, and (d) preserves quota semantics for per-origin and per-customer limits. This ticket covers design, simulation harness, implementation of ledger changes, and rollout safeguards for non-chat embeddings / rerank / structured-output pipelines with tool calls.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by Billing + Serving + Platform (link included)
Billing simulation shows <0.5% expected overcharge on representative workloads vs current baseline while reducing customer-visible double-bills to 0% in simulated duplicate-delivery scenarios

Server/runtime emits a deterministic charge event for finalized executions and a provisional event for speculative work; downstream reconciliation flow reliably converts provisional -> final or issues a credit
Idempotency reconciliation handles duplicate RPC delivery across retry windows: no duplicate invoice lines for same logical request ID
Integration tests added to billing-harness with synthetic fanout + conditional toolcall scenarios; all tests green in CI
Gradual rollout plan defined with metrics and automatic rollback thresholds
technical_notes: Introduce two event types in ledger: 'provisional_charge' (fraction, metadata: origin_id, request_log_id, confidence_score) and 'settled_charge' (final token count, model, route).

Confidence model: use runtime heuristics to map likelihood of eventual execution to fraction charged. Heuristics include: number of downstream conditions evaluated, time-to-first-toolcall, retry_count, and whether KV-cache hit avoided work.
On reconciliation: when settled_charge arrives, compare to any prior provisional_charge(s) by request_log_id and issue delta charge or credit. Credits must preserve invoice-proof lineage.

Idempotency keys: rely on existing request_id + serve_instance signature. For cross-process duplicates, a compact canonicalization (sha256 of canonical request fields) is used to dedupe before emitting a provisional_charge.

Quota semantics: provisional_charge counts toward soft quotas (alerts and temporary reservation) but not hard-enforced hard-limits; only settled_charge decrements hard quota buckets. This prevents speculative attempts from blocking real traffic while still providing backpressure signals.
Edge cases: in-airgap/private deployments, reconciliation messages may be delayed; provisional entries include TTL and after expiry a credit policy runs (auto-refund after expiry if un-settled).

Storage changes: add provisional_charge table with indices on request_log_id, origin_id. Reconciliation worker processes a reconciliation queue with idempotency and at-most-once semantics backed by lease tokens.

Performance: provisional bookkeeping is compact (8-12 bytes of metadata per provisional event) and is batched in the write path to avoid per-request I/O stalls. Batching window default 50ms configurable by tenant tier.
Telemetry: new metrics - provisional_count, provisional_to_settled_ratio, provisional_credit_rate, duplicate_dedupe_rate. Dashboard in Console-ops will track customer-facing deltas.

API/SDK changes: server will continue to return previous usage headers, but a new header X-Redwood-Provisional-Id will be included for requests that generated provisional charges to allow clients to correlate and surface temporary billing notifications.
progress_updates: 2026-02-20 - Ticket created by Sofia; initial problem statement and scope added.

2026-02-25 - Spike completed: small simulator (python) modeling conditional toolcalls created; baseline overcharge observed at 4.2% on sample trace set. (link: drive/confluence/billing-spikes/simulator)

2026-03-01 - Design draft posted to Confluence; solicited feedback from Serving runtime and Platform (meeting notes attached). Key trade-off: whether provisional charges should affect hard quotas. Consensus: provisional -> soft quota only.
2026-03-06 - Implemented provisional_charge schema and a reconciliation worker prototype in the billing sandbox; local integration tests for dedupe pass.

2026-03-10 - End-to-end test against synthetic fanout + 50% conditional toolcall probability; provisional->settled reconciliation path exercised; observed 98.7% reduction in customer-visible duplicate line items in sim.
2026-03-13 - Began PR for runtime changes (WIP). Metric instrumentation added; dashboards prepared. Preparing QA plan for staging rollout.
review_feedback: 2026-03-02 - From Maya (Platform): prefer explicit TTL for provisional entries configurable per-tenant; added to design.
2026-03-04 - From Raj (Billing): ensure credits preserve original invoice line identifiers to allow audit tracing; Raj requested that credit events include original provisional_id.
2026-03-08 - From Elena (Legal): require disclosure in TOS/usage docs for provisional charging behavior; added a docs action item for Legal/Policy review.
2026-03-11 - From Owen (Serving): suggested using existing KV-cache hit flag in heuristics to reduce provisional issuance on cache hits — accepted.
2026-03-12 - From QA lead (Anika): end-to-end failure mode test needed where reconciliation messages are delayed >72h (simulate network partitions); added to test_plan.
test_plan: Unit tests for provisional_charge -> settled_charge reconciliation logic (edge cases: multiple provisional entries for same request_log_id, out-of-order settle events)
Integration tests in billing-harness: simulate 10k requests with randomized toolcall branching and network retry patterns; assert no double charges and expected credit issuance rates.
Chaos test: inject delayed reconciliation messages for a subset of tenants and verify auto-refund TTL behavior and metrics reflect pending provisional backlog.
Performance test: ensure provisional bookkeeping write path adds <1ms p99 tail latency at 10k rps in staging.
Audit test: generate sample invoices and verify lineage from provisional events through credits in invoice viewer UI.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (staging): enable feature flag for internal tenants only; run simulator trace and monitor provisional_count metrics and reconciliation success.
Stage 2 (canary): enable for 5% of production traffic on hosted API (low-volume tenants). Monitor key metrics for 48h: customer-visible credit rate, duplicate invoice deltas, quota anomalies.
Rollback criteria: >0.5% of customers experience unexpected hard-quota exhaustion attributable to provisional charges OR >0.2% increase in billing disputes in 24h.
Stage 3 (gradual ramp): 25% -> 60% -> 100% over 2 weeks with per-step guardrails and automated rollback hooks.
Communication: update docs + customer-facing billing FAQ and send an email to top-20 billing customers describing provisional semantics before 25% ramp.
